name: Monarch Butterfly
description: 4,800 km migration completed across 4 generations. Time-compensated sun compass integrates circadian clock with antenna magnetoreception. Complete metamorphosis reorganizes neural architecture while inherited navigation memory persists.

core_attributes.pattern: multi-generational navigation, complete metamorphosis, inherited spatial memory

scope.definition: Fraction of monarch butterflies arriving within 100 km of overwintering sites in central Mexico after a 4500 km migration performed by individuals with no prior migration experience.

evidence.source: Urquhart & Urquhart (1978) monarch migration tagging studies; Brower (1995) 'Understanding and misunderstanding the migration of the monarch butterfly', Journal of the Lepidopterist Society 49:304-385.
cross_domain_examples: monarch autumn migration 4500 km completed by 3rd-4th generation that never made the journey before
European eels: transoceanic migration to Sargasso Sea spawning grounds with no parental guidance
Arctic tern annual migration 70,000 km — longest known animal migration using inherited route

scope.falsifiability: If marked monarch butterflies reared in isolation without exposure to experienced adults show random dispersal rather than directed southwesterly migration, genetic encoding of route direction fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Navigation accuracy is time-compensated — disruption of circadian clock by constant light leads to random flight direction. Climate change has shifted timing by 2-3 weeks, degrading arrival accuracy.

scope.definition: Accuracy of monarch sun-compass bearing correction across 6 hours of solar movement — deviation from expected bearing when antennae (circadian clock) are experimentally phase-shifted by 6 hours.

evidence.source: Reppert et al. (2010) 'Navigational mechanisms of migrating monarch butterflies', Trends in Neurosciences 33:399-406; Froy et al. (2003) 'Illuminating the circadian clock in monarch butterfly migration', Science 300:1303.
cross_domain_examples: clock-shifted monarchs deviate ~90° from normal migration bearing — proportional to clock shift
UV-sensitive photoreceptors in monarch compound eye provide polarized light compass backup
homing pigeons: same time-compensated sun compass mechanism independently evolved in vertebrates

scope.falsifiability: If clock-shifted monarchs maintain correct migration bearing despite time shift, the sun-compass time-compensation model is incorrect.
scope.measurement_limits: Time-compensation only functions when sun is visible. Overcast days trigger magnetic compass fallback. The 6-hour phase shift produces predictable 90° error — strong mechanistic evidence.

scope.definition: Proportion of larval neural structures (axons, ganglia) that survive metamorphosis and are functionally incorporated into adult nervous system, versus being destroyed and rebuilt.

evidence.source: Bhaskara et al. (2009) neural reorganization during metamorphosis; Truman & Reiss (1988) 'Hormonal regulation of the shape of identified motoneurons', Journal of Neuroscience 8:765-775.
cross_domain_examples: mushroom body Kenyon cells persist through metamorphosis and rewire to adult olfactory system
larval memory of trained avoidance behavior partially retained through metamorphosis in some studies
axolotl limb regeneration: dedifferentiation and redifferentiation maintain limb motor map — partial analogue

scope.falsifiability: If all larval neural structures are shown to be completely destroyed during histolysis (no measurable continuity), adult monarchs have no substrate for any larval memory.
scope.measurement_limits: Neural persistence varies by structure type: some larval motor neurons survive while most sensory neurons are rebuilt. Learned behavior retention through metamorphosis remains experimentally contested.
